html:
SMTO-GML-0021 — Too many Gmail sign-ins are waiting to be finished

GUID: 7e77a75c-c4fc-4e08-a7fc-773ca88c1450
Slug: gmail-oauth-too-many-pending
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Many Gmail sign-ins were started but not finished, and SMTO only allows a limited number at once. SMTO didn't start a new one. Nothing about your connected accounts changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you have a Google sign-in window still open from SMTO, finish it by choosing your account and selecting Allow. Finishing a waiting sign-in frees up a place and may already connect your account.
  2. Otherwise, wait about 10 minutes without starting any new Gmail connections. Unfinished sign-ins expire after 10 minutes and SMTO then clears them.
  3. Then ask SMTO once to connect your Gmail account and complete that sign-in. Starting many connections in a row is what filled the list in the first place.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a new Google sign-in link, and after you approve it the Google window says your account is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, especially if this happens when you haven't started many sign-ins; something may be starting them repeatedly. Don't keep clicking connect while you wait.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • BrowserOAuth.start refused a new Gmail authorization because at least 32 unexpired pending OAuth handshakes already exist after expiring old ones.

What this means

  • BrowserOAuth.start expires old handshakes then finds at least 32 pending authorizations before admitting another. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • BrowserOAuth.start expires old handshakes then finds at least 32 pending authorizations before admitting another.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect pending flow count and ownership instead of opening more windows.

How to fix it

  • BrowserOAuth.start purges expired handshakes (10-minute lifetime) and raises gmail_oauth_too_many_pending when 32 or more remain in its in-memory pending map. Complete or abandon outstanding flows and wait for them to expire, and look for an automation or retry loop that repeatedly calls gmail.connect or POST /api/agent/gmail/auth/start.
  • Let pending flows complete or expire before starting another authorization.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing flows complete/expire and one intended new authorization can be admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
